Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 40, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called Ghafir (the Forgiver), because Allah, glory be to Him, mentions at its beginning this great attribute, which is one of His attributes, and it is not mentioned in any other place.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Challenging the obstinate ones to establish the truthfulness of the Qur'an, and clarifying that disputing about the Qur'an by those who dispute is nothing but sowing confusion and envy, and calling people to abandon their obstinacy, argumentation and denial, and warning the deniers and obstinate ones who dispute the signs of Allah.

• Discussing some scenes of the Resurrection and its terrors: the people's being brought forth before Allah, hearts reaching the throats, and discussing the criminals as they argue in the Fire of Hell, and depicting their condition in the Fire as humiliated, asking the guardians of Hell (khazanah) to pray to Allah to lighten their punishment.

• Mention of the story of Musa (Moses) with Fir'awn (Pharaoh), in which the stance of tyranny and arrogance toward the call to truth is represented, and an example of how the believer should be in admonishing his people, in the story of the believer from the family of Fir'awn, who proclaims the word of truth with gentleness, caution and variety in admonition.

• Mention of the cosmic signs that point to the greatness of this universe and testify to the oneness and power of the Creator, and the argument for the possibility of resurrection, and the presentation of parables for the believer and the disbeliever.

• Clarification of the fates of the deniers and tyrants, whom Allah seized with the seizure of the Mighty, the Powerful, and the depiction of the condition of those who deny the Prophet (ﷺ) by the condition of the nations who denied the messengers of Allah before them.

[Tafsir]

﴿Ḥā Mīm﴾ The discussion of the disjointed letters has already been given at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah.
The revelation of the Qur'an to the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) is from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the Almighty who by His might subdued every creature, the All-Knowing of everything.

The Forgiver of sin, and the Acceptor of repentance, severe in punishment against those who dare to commit sins and do not repent from them. He, glorified and exalted is He, is the Possessor of bounty and favor toward His obedient servants. There is no deity worthy of worship besides Him. To Him is the return of all creation on the Day of Reckoning, and He will recompense each according to what they deserve.

None dispute the verses of the Qur'an and its proofs of Allah's oneness, opposing them with falsehood, except the deniers who reject that He is the true God, deserving of worship alone. So do not be deceived, O Messenger, by their movement throughout the lands in various kinds of trade and gain, and by the bliss and splendor of this worldly life.

The commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 40, verse 5:

Before these disbelievers, the people of Noah and the nations that came after them, such as ʿAd and Thamud, denied their messengers. They declared war upon the messengers, resolved to harm them, and gathered against them to torment or kill them. Every nation that denied its messenger was determined to kill him, and they argued with falsehood in order to nullify the truth through their disputation. So I seized them with punishment. How, then, was My punishment of them? It was a lesson for creation and a warning for those who would come after them.
And just as the punishment was decreed against the earlier nations that denied their messengers, it is decreed against those who disbelieve, that they are the companions of the Fire.

Those who carry the Throne of the Most Merciful, from among the angels, and those around the Throne who encircle it, glorify Allah, exalting Him above every imperfection, and praise Him with the praise that befits Him. They believe in Him with true faith, and they ask Him to pardon the believers, saying: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who have repented from polytheism and sins, and who have followed the path You commanded them to follow, which is Islam, and protect them from the punishment of the Fire and its terrors.﴾

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 40, verse 8:**

﴿Our Lord, admit them into the Gardens of Eden which You promised them, along with whoever was righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring. Indeed, You are the Mighty, the Subduer of all things, the Wise in His management and His creation.﴾

And ward off from them the evil consequences of their misdeeds, so that You do not punish them for them. Whoever You ward off from evil deeds on the Day of Reckoning, You have indeed shown him mercy and bestowed upon him deliverance from Your punishment, and that is the great triumph, for which there is no equal success.

Indeed, those who disbelieved, denying that Allah is the true God and directing worship to other than Him, when they witness the horrors of the Fire with their own eyes, will loathe themselves with the utmost loathing. At that moment, the keepers of Hell (khazanat Jahannam) will call out to them: "The loathing of Allah toward you in the worldly life, when He called you to faith in Him and to follow His messengers, and you refused, was greater than your loathing of yourselves now, after you have come to realize that you deserve the wrath and punishment of Allah."

The Unbelievers will say: "Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and gave us life twice. The first death was when we were drops of sperm in our mothers' wombs before the soul was breathed into us, and the second was when our term in this worldly life came to an end. The first life was in this worldly abode, the day we were born, and the second was the day we were raised from our graves. So now we acknowledge our past sins. Is there any way for us to get out of the Fire and be returned to the world, so that we may act in obedience to You?" But this acknowledgment will not benefit them; it is too late.

That punishment is yours, you disbelievers, because when you were called to the Oneness of God and to making worship sincerely for Him alone, you disbelieved in Him; but when a partner is set up for God, you affirmed it and followed it. So God, glorified and exalted, is the Judge over His creation, the Just who does not oppress. He guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills, and He has mercy on whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. There is no god but Him, the One to whom belong supreme exaltation in essence, rank and dominance, and to whom belong greatness and majesty.
He it is who shows you His signs, and sends down for you provisions from the sky. And none remembers except one who turns back (to obedience of Allah) and devotes worship sincerely to Him.
Then, O believers, devote your worship and supplication sincerely to Allah alone, and oppose the polytheists in their way, even if that angers them, and do not concern yourselves with them.

Indeed, Allah is the Most High, the Exalted, whose ranks are raised in a manner distinct from His creation, and by whom His station is elevated. He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne. And of His mercy toward His servants is that He sends to them messengers, to whom He casts down the revelation by which they are given life, so that they may be upon insight regarding their affair; that the messengers may warn the servants of Allah and admonish them concerning the Day of Resurrection, the Day on which the first and the last will meet.

On the Day of Resurrection, all creatures will appear before their Lord. Nothing concerning them, nor concerning their deeds which they performed in the world, is hidden from Allah. Allah, glorified is He, says: "To whom belongs the dominion and authority on this Day?" Then He answers Himself: "To Allah, the One who is singular in His names, His attributes and His actions, the Subduer (al-Qahhar) who has subdued all creatures by His power and might."

Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned in the world, whether good or evil. There is no injustice today: no one will have any of his evil deeds increased, nor any of his good deeds diminished. Indeed, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is swift in reckoning, so do not regard that Day as far off, for it is near.

Warn them, O Messenger, of the Imminent Day (the Day of Resurrection), even though they consider it distant. On that Day, the hearts of the servants, from fear of God's punishment, will rise up from their chests and lodge in their throats, while they are filled with distress and grief. The wrongdoers will have no close friend and no companion, nor any intercessor who will intercede for them with their Lord so that his intercession is accepted.
God, glory be to Him, knows the glances that eyes steal, and what a person conceals within himself of good or evil.

Allah judges between people with justice concerning what they deserve. As for those who are worshipped besides Allah, the false deities, they judge nothing, because they are incapable of that. Indeed, Allah is the All-Hearing of His creatures' statements, the All-Seeing of their deeds and actions, and He will recompense them for them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 40, verse 21:

Have these deniers of your message, O Messenger, not traveled through the land and seen how the final outcome was for the nations before them? They were stronger than them in might, and left more lasting traces upon the earth, yet the strength of their power and the greatness of their bodies did not benefit them. So Allah seized them with His punishment, because of their disbelief and their earning of sins, and they had no protector from the punishment of Allah to shield them from it and ward it off from them.

That punishment which befell the earlier deniers was because of their stance toward God's messengers, who came with clear proofs of the truth of their claim. So they disbelieved in them and denied them, and God seized them with His punishment. Indeed, He, glorified is He, is Mighty; none can overcome Him, and He is severe in punishment toward whoever disbelieves in Him and disobeys Him.

And We certainly sent Musa (Moses) with Our great signs, which point to the truth of what he was sent with, and with clear, manifest proof of his truthfulness in his call, and of the falsehood of what those to whom he was sent were upon.

To Pharaoh, king of "Egypt," and Haman, his minister, and Qarun (Korah), the possessor of wealth and treasures. So they denied his message and grew arrogant, and they said of him: "He is a sorcerer and a liar. How can he claim that he has been sent to the people as a messenger?"

When Moses came to Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun with the clear miracles from Us, they did not content themselves with opposing and denying them, but said: "Kill the sons of those who believe with him, and spare their women for service and enslavement." And the scheming of the disbelievers is nothing but going astray and destruction.

Pharaoh said to the nobles of his people: "Leave me to kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord, whom he claims has sent him to us. Let him see whether his Lord will protect him from us. Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion, which you follow, or that he will cause corruption to appear in the land of Egypt."

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 40, verse 27:**

Moses said to Pharaoh and his chiefs: "Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord, O people, from every arrogant one who is too proud to affirm the Oneness of Allah and to obey Him, and who does not believe in the Day on which Allah will call His creation to account."

And a man of the family of Pharaoh, a believer who concealed his faith, said, rebuking his people: "Will you kill a man merely because he says, 'My Lord is Allah,' when he has brought you clear proofs from your Lord to the truth of what he says? And if he is a liar, then the harm of his lying falls upon him alone; but if he is truthful, some of what he threatens you with will befall you. Indeed, Allah does not guide to the truth one who is a transgressor, one who abandons the truth and turns to falsehood, a liar who attributes to Allah what he has exceeded in."

O my people, the dominion is yours today, as you prevail in the land of Egypt over your subjects among the Children of Israel and others. But who will protect us from the punishment of Allah should it befall us?" Pharaoh said to his people in reply: "I show you only what I see as right and good for myself and for you, and I call you only to the path of truth and rectitude."

The believing man from the family of Pharaoh said to Pharaoh and his chiefs, admonishing and warning: "I fear for you that if you kill Musa, [you will suffer] a fate like that of the day of the factions, those who formed factions against their prophets."

Like the custom of the people of Noah, ʿĀd, Thamūd, and those who came after them in disbelief and denial, God destroyed them because of that. And God, glorified is He, does not desire injustice for His servants, so as to punish them without a sin they committed. Exalted is God above injustice and deficiency, a great exaltation.
And O my people, indeed I fear for you the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, the Day when people will call out to one another, because of the terror of that standing.

The Day you turn your backs and flee, you will have no protector from Allah to shield you, and no helper to support you. And whomever Allah leaves to go astray, not granting him guidance to his right path, he has no guide to lead him to the truth and what is right.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 40, verse 34:

Indeed, Allah sent to you Yusuf son of Ya'qub (peace be upon them both), the noble Prophet, before Musa, with clear proofs of his truthfulness. He commanded you to worship Allah alone, without partner, but you continued in doubt about what he brought you during his lifetime. When he died, your doubt and your polytheism increased, and you said: "Allah will never send after him any messenger." Thus does Allah lead astray everyone who transgresses the truth and doubts the oneness of Allah, the Exalted, so He does not guide him to right guidance and rectitude.

Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah and His proofs, seeking to refute them without any acceptable evidence they possess, such disputation is greatly hateful in the sight of Allah and in the sight of those who believe. Just as Allah sealed the hearts of these disputers, causing them to be led astray and barring them from guidance, so Allah seals the heart of every arrogant person who turns away from the Oneness of Allah and His obedience, the tyrant who is overbearing through his abundant wrongdoing and transgression.

Pharaoh said, rejecting Moses in his call to acknowledge the Lord of the worlds and submit to Him: "O Haman, build for me a lofty tower, so that perhaps I may reach the passageways of the heavens and look upon the God of Moses. Indeed, I think he is a liar in his claim that we have a Lord and that He is above the heavens." Thus was the evil of Pharaoh made attractive to him, and he saw it as good, and he was turned away from the path of truth, because of the falsehood with which he was adorned. And the scheming and plotting of Pharaoh, by which he sought to make people imagine that he is in the right and Moses is in the wrong, will bring him nothing but loss and ruin, yielding him only misery in this world and in the Hereafter.

And the scheming and plotting of Pharaoh, by which he sought to make people imagine that he is in the right and Moses is in the wrong, will bring him nothing but loss and ruin, yielding him only misery in this world and in the Hereafter.
And the one who had believed said, repeating his advice to his people: "O my people, follow me, and I will guide you to the path of right guidance and correctness."

O my people, this worldly life is only a brief enjoyment for people, and then it ends and passes away. So you should not incline toward it. Indeed, the Hereafter, with its everlasting bliss, is the abode of permanence where you will settle, so you should prefer it and do the righteous deeds that will make you happy there.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 40, verse 40:

Whoever disobeys Allah in his life and deviates from the path of guidance, he will not be recompensed in the Hereafter except with a punishment equal to his disobedience. And whoever obeys Allah and does righteous deeds, by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, whether male or female, while he is a believer in Allah, affirming His oneness, those will enter Paradise, and Allah will provide them therein with its fruits, its blessings and its pleasures without reckoning.

O my people, how is it that I call you to faith in God and to following His messenger Musa (Moses), a call that leads you to Paradise and keeps you far from the terrors of the Fire, while you call me to a deed that leads to the punishment of God and His chastisement in the Fire?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 40, verse 42:

You call me to disbelieve in Allah and to associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge, that it deserves worship besides Him—and this is among the greatest and most abominable of sins—while I call you to the path that leads to Allah, the Mighty in His retribution, the Forgiving to whoever repents to Him after his disobedience.

Truly, that to which you invite me to believe does not deserve to be called upon, nor sought as a refuge, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter, because of its incapacity and deficiency. And know that the final return of all creatures is to Allah, the Glorified, and He will recompense every doer for his deeds, and that those who transgress His limits through sins, the shedding of blood, and disbelief, they are the companions of the Fire.

So when he advised them and they did not obey him, he said to them: "You will remember that I gave you sincere counsel and reminded you, and you will regret when regret will not benefit you. I take refuge in Allah, seek protection in Him, and put my trust in Him. Indeed, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is All-Seeing of the conditions of His servants and of the recompense they deserve; nothing of it is hidden from Him."

God, exalted is He, protected that believing man, who was granted success, from the consequences of the schemes of Pharaoh and his household. The evil torment befell them, as God drowned them all to the last one.

The commentary on surah 40, verse 46 (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, King Fahd Complex):

They were first struck by drowning and perished. Then they are punished in their graves, where the Fire is; they are presented to it morning and evening until the time of reckoning. And on the day the Hour is established, it will be said: "Admit the people of Pharaoh into the most severe punishment," as recompense for the evil deeds they committed. This verse is a foundation for establishing the punishment of the grave.

﴿And mention when the people of the Fire will dispute with one another in the Fire, and the weak among them will say to those who were arrogant: "Indeed, we were your followers, so will you then relieve us of a portion of the Fire?"﴾

Note that the passage above has been rendered as a translation of the verse itself, which was not the intent. The correct translation of the commentary is as follows:

When the people of the Fire dispute and blame one another, the followers who blindly imitated argue against their arrogant leaders who misled them and made the path of wretchedness appear attractive to them, saying to them: "Will you bear for us a share of the Fire by taking on a portion of our punishment?"

The arrogant leaders said, making clear their helplessness: "We will not bear for you any part of the punishment of the Fire, for all of us are in it, and there is no escape for us from it. Indeed, Allah has apportioned the punishment among us in accordance with what each of us deserves by His just decree."
Those in the Fire, among the arrogant and the weak, will say to the keepers of Hell: "Call upon your Lord to lighten the punishment for us by one day, so that we may gain some relief."

The keepers of Hell say to them, rebuking them: "This supplication will not benefit you in anything. Did your messengers not come to you with clear proofs from Allah, and you denied them?" The deniers acknowledge this and say: "Yes." Then the keepers of Hell disassociate themselves from them and say: "We do not supplicate for you, nor intercede for you. So supplicate yourselves, but this supplication will not avail anything, because you are disbelievers. And the supplication of the disbelievers is nothing but in vain; it is not accepted and not answered."

We surely help Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the day when the witnesses stand forth, the day when the angels, the prophets and the believers will bear witness against the peoples who denied their messengers. They will testify that the messengers had indeed conveyed the messages of their Lord, and that those peoples had denied them.

On the Day of Reckoning, the disbelievers who transgressed the bounds of Allah will gain nothing from the excuses they offer for denying Allah's messengers. For them is expulsion from the mercy of Allah, and for them is the evil abode in the Hereafter, which is the Fire.

We certainly gave Musa (Moses) that which guides to the truth: the Torah and the miracles. And We made the Children of Israel inherit the Torah, generation after generation, as a guidance to the path of righteousness and an admonition for people of sound minds.

We certainly gave Musa (Moses) that which guides to the truth: the Torah and the miracles. And We made the Children of Israel inherit the Torah, generation after generation, as a guidance to the path of righteousness and an admonition for people of sound minds.

So be patient, O Messenger, over the harm inflicted by the polytheists, for We have promised you the elevation of your word, and Our promise is true and will not be broken. Seek forgiveness for your sin, and continue to glorify your Lord, exalting Him above whatever is unfitting for Him, at the end of the day and at its beginning.

Indeed, those who dispute the truth with falsehood, and who reject sound proofs with corrupt doubts, without any evidence or authority from God, there is nothing in their breasts but arrogance toward the truth, out of envy at the favour that God has bestowed upon His Prophet and the honour of prophethood with which He has honoured him. Yet it is a matter they will never attain or reach. So seek refuge in God from their evil; indeed, He is the All-Hearing of their words, the All-Seeing of their deeds, and He will recompense them for them.

The creation of the heavens and the earth by God is greater than the creation of mankind and their resurrection after their death; but most people do not know that the creation of all of that is easy for God.

The blind and the seeing are not alike, and likewise the believers who acknowledge that Allah is the true God with no partner, who respond to His messengers and act by His law, are not alike to the deniers who reject that Allah is the true God, who deny His messengers, and who do not act by His law. Little do you remember, O people, the proofs of Allah, so that you may take heed and be admonished by them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 40, verse 59:

Indeed, the Hour is surely coming, there is no doubt about it, so be certain of its arrival, as the messengers have informed. But most people do not believe in its coming, nor do they prepare for it.

And your Lord said, (O servants): "Call upon Me alone, and single Me out for worship, and I will respond to you." Indeed, those who are too proud to devote worship and divinity solely to Me will enter Hell, humbled and debased.

It is Allah alone who made the night for you, so that you may rest in it and attain your comfort, and the day bright, so that you may conduct the affairs of your livelihood in it. Indeed, Allah is full of great bounty toward mankind, but most of them do not give Him thanks through obedience and sincere worship.

That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things. There is no deity worthy of worship besides Him. So how are you turned away from believing in Him and worshipping others, idols, after its proofs have become clear to you?

Just as you (O disbelievers of Quraysh) denied the truth and turned away from it toward falsehood, so are turned away from the truth and from belief in it those who used to reject the proofs and evidences of God.

Allah is the One who made the earth a resting place for you, and made it easy for you to dwell upon it, and made the sky a canopy over the earth, and scattered within it signs that guide. He created you in the most complete form and the finest proportion, and bestowed upon you lawful provision and delicious foods and drinks. That is your Lord, who has bestowed these blessings upon you; abundant is His goodness, His bounty, and His blessing, and He is exalted above whatever is not befitting to Him. He is the Lord of all creation.

He is Allah, the Ever-Living, who possesses perfect and complete life. There is no god but Him. So call upon Him alone, directing your worship to Him alone, sincerely devoting your religion and obedience to Him. All praise is due to Allah, and complete commendation belongs to Him, the Lord of all creation.

Say, O Messenger, to the polytheists of your people: "Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides Allah, now that clear proofs have come to me from my Lord. And He has commanded me to submit and to surrender in complete obedience to Him, exalted is He, the Lord of the worlds."

He is God, who created your father Adam from dust, then brought you into being from semen by His power. After that you pass into the stage of thick red blood clot, then various stages are successively undergone by you in the wombs, until you are born as small children. Then your bodies grow strong until you become elderly, and among you is one who dies before that. This is so that you may reach, through these predetermined stages, a specified term at which your lifespans end, and so that perhaps you will understand the proofs of God against you in this, and reflect upon His signs, and thus know that there is no god but Him who does this, and that He alone is the One to whom worship is due.
He (Allah, glorified is He) is the One who alone gives life and causes death. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is. None can turn back His decree.

Do you not marvel, O Messenger, at those who deny the signs of God and dispute concerning them, though they are clear in their indication of God's oneness and power? How do they turn away from them despite their soundness? And to what do they go after such complete clarity?

These disbelievers who denied the Qur'an and the heavenly scriptures that Allah sent down through His messengers to guide mankind will come to know the consequence of their denial, when shackles will be placed around their necks and chains upon their feet, and the angels of punishment (al-zabaniyah) will drag them through scalding water whose boiling and heat have intensified, and then they will be burned in the Fire of Hell.

The deniers will say: "They have vanished from our sight, and they have benefited us in nothing." That punishment which has befallen you is only because of what you were upon in your worldly life of heedlessness, when you used to rejoice in the sins and wrongdoings you committed, and in your insolence, arrogance, and transgression against the servants of Allah.

Enter the gates of Hell, as a punishment for you for your disbelief in God and your disobedience to Him, abiding in it forever. How evil is Hell as a lodging for those who were arrogant in the world toward God.

Therefore be patient, O Messenger, and continue on the path of the call. Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, and He will fulfill for you what He has promised. So whether We show you in your lifetime some of what We threaten these polytheists with of punishment, or We take you (in death) before that befalls them, then to Us is their return on the Day of Resurrection, and We will make them taste the severe punishment because of what they used to disbelieve.

And We have certainly sent messengers before you, O Messenger, many of them, to their peoples, calling them and enduring their harm. Among them are those whose stories We have related to you, and among them are those whose stories We have not related to you. All of them were commanded to convey the revelation of Allah to them. It was not for any of them to bring a sign of the signs, whether sensory or intellectual, except by the permission of Allah and His will. So when the command of Allah comes concerning the punishment of the deniers, judgment is passed with justice between the messengers and their deniers, and there the falsifiers will lose, because of their fabrication against Allah of falsehood and their worship of other than Him.

Allah, glory be to Him, is the One who made the grazing livestock (al-an'am) for you, so that you may benefit from them: from their uses for riding and eating, and other kinds of benefit, and so that by means of their loads you may reach a need in your hearts, namely arriving at distant lands. Upon these livestock you are carried on land, and upon ships you are carried likewise on the sea.

Allah shows you His many clear signs, which point to His power and His management of His creation. So which of His signs do you deny, failing to acknowledge them?

Have these deniers not traveled through the earth and considered the fate of the nations that denied before them? How was their outcome? These earlier nations were more numerous than them, greater in strength, and greater in their traces upon the earth, in buildings, factories, and plantations, and other things. Yet what they had earned did not avail them when the punishment of God came upon them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 40, verse 83:

When those disbelieving nations were visited by their messengers with clear proofs, they exulted in their ignorance, because of the knowledge they had which contradicted what the messengers had brought. And there befell them the punishment that they used to mock and ridicule when they hastened it upon their messengers. In the verse there is evidence that every knowledge which contradicts Islam, or disparages it, or casts doubt upon its validity, is blameworthy and detested, and whoever holds it is not among the followers of Muhammad (ﷺ).

When they saw Our punishment, they acknowledged the truth at a time when acknowledgment no longer benefited them, and they said: "We believe in Allah alone, and we reject what we used to associate with Him in worship."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 40, verse 85:

So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment. That is because it was a faith to which they were compelled, not a faith of choice and willingness. It is the way of Allah, His established practice among all nations, that faith does not benefit them once they have seen the punishment. And there perished at the coming of Allah's might the disbelievers in their Lord, those who denied His Oneness and refused to obey Him.
